LESSON: READING 3.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: LIBRARY SKILLS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills, part of Strand 3 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we make use of the library resources well? 2. How have you engaged yourself in serving your community and society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to collect varied reading resources on people who have served their communities well and successfully,

2. organise the reading resources in the class portfolio,

3. work with peers to discuss key considerations

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to collect varied reading resources on people who have served their communities well and successfully,
2. organise the reading resources in the class portfolio,
3. work with peers to discuss key considerations

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Extensive Reading: Library skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: The learner accumulates varied reading resources on people who have served their communities well and

successfully.

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: The learner explores views when discussing key considerations when using the

library.

Values:
• Respect: It is enhanced as the learner ensures positive regard for others when conducting a silent reading session to read

resources and grade appropriate texts.

• Patriotism: This is promoted as the learner is devoted to working with peers to collect varied reading resources on people

who have served their communities well and successfully.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Civic Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner collaborates with peers to come up with a reading club for indigenous

languages materials.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the skills acquired in extensive reading to their independent reading in Religious Studies.
